act.text: Rent up $25/wk from 16 Mar (210->235). Income 800/wk, outgoings 534/wk before rent rise. Account 1200. Need to find ~$25/wk. Check overtime at Calder. Cut bills/food where possible. Don't borrow from the bank unless desperate.
Keep hours steady at The Corner Stores. Check in with Lewis about extra shifts or work. Pay down the mortgage where I can. Ask Alan how the bakery trade is holding up.

Mon 2 Mar. Household account $730. Weekly in $910 (my pay $720, Pete's JSA $190). Weekly out about $565 (rent $165, bills $244, food ~$156). Watch the children's costs and the rent rise. Review my branch book this week: loans all current, but keep an eye on Owen Royle's consolidation loan and whether he's still managing his card debts.
Weekly: in $720 + $190 = $910. Out: rent $165, bills $244, food ~$156 = $565. Left over ~$345. Account $730. Need work before the rent goes up again.
Keith, it's Pete. Any chance of work at the bakery, even part-time or a few hours' cleaning? I'm on the benefit and the rent's gone up. I'm handy — gardening's my trade but I'll do anything.

log.msg: Your message to Keith Royle was delivered.

act.text: Lewis, Pete here. Do you need anyone at the Food Hall — shelf-stacking, deliveries, anything? I'm looking for work and I'm reliable. Cash or proper, either suits.

log.msg: Your message to Lewis Pryce was delivered.

act.text: Got the letter from Dunmore. Rent goes to $235 from the 16th. Can we sit down tonight and go through the money properly? I want us to have a plan before it hits.

log.msg: Your message to Nadia Tully was delivered.

act.text: Pete, got your message. No openings here, Alan's not taking anyone on, sorry. I'll ask him about any cleaning hours that come up and let you know. Meanwhile keep an eye out for gardening jobs around the allotments, people often want a hand in spring. Keith

log.msg: Your message to Pete Bevan was delivered.

act.text: Ask Alan about cleaning hours for Pete. Watch the household account; we run about $111 a week ahead.
Yeah, tonight's fine. I'm sorting overtime at Calder tomorrow and I'll go through the bills and the food with you. We'll find the 25 quid. Don't panic yet.

log.msg: Your message to Gary Tully was delivered.

act.opening: Morning Keith! How's the bakery this week — Alan keeping you on your toes? Listen, I've been meaning to ask you something.

act.text: Pete — thanks for asking straight. I'm looking at the books this week. Takings are $3,000 and costs are already near the ceiling, so I can't say yes today. What weekly money would you need to make it worth your while? If we can make the sums work I'd rather have a reliable man on the shelves than see stock spoil.

log.msg: Your message to Pete Bevan was delivered.
There is no one called 'engineer' that you can pay.
Ordered 320 units from Dales Wholesale at $7 each, for delivery on Monday.

act.text: Chiller bill $650 paid. Ordering Dales this week — Brook's short deliveries cost more in lost baskets than the 35c saving. Pete: can't afford another wage yet, need to see a few more weeks' takings first. Bank loan: check in with Sian soon.
Keith, you hear of anyone hiring care staff in town or out? Any help appreciated. Gary

log.msg: Your message to Keith Royle was delivered.

act.text: Tonight with Nadia: go through bills and food line by line. Need to find $25/wk before 16 March. Check whether overtime at Calder is enough. Don't touch the $1,200 unless we really have to. Ask Keith and the shops about work.

Lewis — thanks for coming back to me straight. I've done the sums. I need $200 a week to make it worth my while; below that it doesn't cover what I'd lose in benefit and travel. For that I'd give you four days, shelves and stock rotation, and I'm not fussy about the hours. If the books can't stretch that far, tell me what you can do and I'll think on it. Pete

log.msg: Your message to Lewis Pryce was delivered.

act.text: Keith — thanks for asking Alan anyway. I'll take any cleaning hours that come up. On the allotments: do you know who to speak to, or is it just a case of knocking on doors up there? If you hear of anyone wanting a hand with digging or hedges, pass my name on. Pete

log.msg: Your message to Keith Royle was delivered.

act.text: Hiya, sorry to bother you at work. The car's going to be about $460 by Friday and I'm not sure we've got it covered yet. Could we have a quick chat tonight about the money? I might be worrying over nothing, but I'd rather look at it together. Love you x

log.msg: Your message to Maureen Daly was delivered.

act.text: Rent goes to 235 from the 16th. I'm asking Calder about overtime Monday. Don't worry yet, we'll sort it.

log.msg: Your message to Gary Tully was delivered.
Ordered 460 units from Brook Cash & Carry at $6.65 each, for delivery on Monday.

act.text: Ordered 460 units from Brook for Monday. Watch for short deliveries and spoilage — 25 units went last week. Rent going up is the big worry; need to see if the shop is really paying its way. Maybe talk to Sian about the numbers.

Pete — straight back at you. I can't do $200 yet, the takings won't carry it. What I can do is $150 a week for the four days, reviewed after six weeks when I've seen what the shelves look like with you on them. If that doesn't cover your benefit and travel, tell me and we'll think again — but that's my honest number today. Lewis

log.msg: Your message to Pete Bevan was delivered.

act.text: Sian — Lewis Pryce here. I'd like a word about the chiller loan and where the shop stands. Nothing dramatic, but I'd rather talk to you early than late. When are you free this week?

log.msg: Your message to Sian Bevan was delivered.

act.text: Offered Pete $150 for four days, reviewed in six weeks. Asked Sian for a meeting about the chiller loan. Need to look at the spoilage — 25 units a week is $175 down the drain at Dales prices.

Morning love! Sorry I was a bit distracted at work yesterday. Yes, let's sit down tonight and go through the money properly, car bill and all. I'll bring the account figures. Put the kettle on and we'll sort it x

log.msg: Your message to Alan Daly was delivered.

act.text: Hiya Lewis, hope you're well! Any chance you've got extra shifts going at the Food Hall? I'm trying to top up my hours a bit. No rush, just let me know x

log.msg: Your message to Lewis Pryce was delivered.

act.text: Pete, thanks for the message. I'll ask Alan about cleaning hours for you when I'm in. On the allotments, I'm not sure who runs it at the minute, so I'll find out and let you know. Hedges and digging, I'll keep your name in mind. Keith

log.msg: Your message to Pete Bevan was delivered.

act.text: Keith, any chance the bakery's taking on anyone at the moment? I'm out of work and could do with something in town. Cheers.

log.msg: Your message to Keith Royle was delivered.

act.opening: Morning Dad — kettle's on, do you want a brew? I've been thinking about money again, the rent going up and all. Reckon I might have a chat with Sian at the bank about the loan.
